主要内容: President Donald Trump announced that the U.S. will suspend funding to the World Health Organization (WHO) while it conducts a review of the agency's response to the coronavirus pandemic. Trump criticized the WHO for its handling of the outbreak, particularly its opposition to travel restrictions from China, which he claimed led to "so much death." The administration plans to conduct a thorough investigation over 60 to 90 days, during which all funds to the WHO will be put on hold. Trump emphasized that the decision is not about the money but about evaluating the WHO's role in the pandemic. The WHO did not immediately respond to the announcement, but UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres stated that reducing resources during the pandemic is not the right time. The move raises questions about how Trump intends to withhold funding, as much of the money is appropriated by Congress, and the president typically lacks unilateral authority to redirect such funds. Trump accused the WHO of promoting misinformation from China, claiming it downplayed the virus's contagiousness and delayed travel bans. The WHO had declared a global health emergency on January 30, nearly a month before Trump claimed the virus was under control in the US. The organization's warning came as the virus spread rapidly, infecting over 1.9 million people and killing at least 125,678 globally.
